translations.title: Ahora, ¿adónde?
translations.text:
Now, where to? My awkward foot
would like to carry me to Germany.
But prudent reason shakes its head,
as if to say:
The war is indeed over,
but courts-martial remain,
and they say you once wrote
things for which you could be shot.
That is true; it would be unpleasant
to see myself executed.
I am no hero; I lack
their pathetic gestures.
I would like to go to England,
if only there were no coal smoke—and the English! Their smell
already makes me retch and vomit.
At times I get the notion
to sail for North America,
great stable of liberty
with its equal-minded brutes.
But I fear a country
of people who chew tobacco,
who, without a king, play bowls,
and spit without spittoons.
Russia, that beautiful empire,
would perhaps please me,
but in winter I could not
endure the beatings there.
Sadly I gaze above,
where thousands of stars wink;
yet my own star
I cannot see anywhere.
Perhaps it was lost
in heaven’s golden maze,
as I myself am lost
in earthly turmoil.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Aquel poderoso hechizo
translations.text:
That powerful enchantment
I shall never forget:
I heard her for the first time,
and her voice was soft music
that presses the heart and clouds the eyes
with sweet tears,
while the soul scarcely notices
the bliss that floods it.
A dream suddenly filled
my bewildered imagination:
in my mother’s room,
lit by a feeble lamp,
a trusting child, I read
fabulous adventures,
while winds whistled
through pale mists.
The fables took on flesh:
the heroes rose from their graves;
at Roncesvalles a mighty battle
burst forth;
Roland rides there,
his armies go there,
and with them goes Ganelon,
may God confound him!
Betrayed by him and wounded,
Roland falls, yet still grips
the horn and brings it to his lips.
Its cry resounds so loudly
that far away it carries
to great Charles his anguish.
Roland dies, and his death
breaks my bloody dream.
A sudden storm of applause
wakes me with a roar:
the powerful spell is over,
the strange adventure ended;
everyone claps and cries
“bravo!” and “hurrah!”
while the singer bows
deeply to the crowd.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: La princesa Ilsa
translations.text:
I am Ilsa, the princess bewitched,
who keeps the river in its mysterious caves.
Come with me to my splendid home,
and we shall be happy and blessed.

Come bathe your troubled, weary brow
in my abundant stream,
and you, young man near death,
will forget life’s bitterness.

Come sleep within my white arms,
come lie upon my white breast;
caught in these bonds, you will dream
of another world, filled with enchantment.

The dam of pleasure and delight now broken,
I will embrace and kiss you eagerly,
as I did glorious Emperor Henry,
my faithful, passionate lover.

But death has sealed his tomb;
he lies motionless in the gloomy bed.
I am capricious, young, and lovely,
and my breast still beats, yearning for love.

Come to my hidden crystal palace:
there, lovers made proud by love
dance with ladies of divine splendor,
while pages sing and laugh.

Silk tunics rustle there,
golden spurs ring;
bright-faced dwarfs play
the deep horn and sonorous drum.

As once I held the glorious emperor,
my burning arms will clasp you;
when the martial trumpet shook him,
I covered his ears with kisses.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Los tejedores de silesta
translations.text:
Silent, faithless, no tears shine
in those men’s dry eyes.
Their teeth grind; they sing funeral songs
seated before the loom:
“Old Germany, your icy shroud
our fingers weave in darkness,
and into the vile cloth our lips mingle
echoes of curses and rage.
We weave! We weave!

“Cursed be the God of the happy,
to whom we raised our wretched cries
through endless days of hunger
and winter’s freezing nights.
In vain we trusted in his mercy;
he sold us out, poor fools!
We weave! We weave!

“Cursed be the king, the rich man’s king,
to whom in vain, hearts bitter,
we begged for mercy and compassion.
He snatched the last coin from our purse
with greed, and now has us
machine-gunned like dogs.
We weave! We weave!

“Cursed be our homeland too,
our German homeland, where heaven
covers only shame, evil, and disgrace;
where the flower opens its petals to the wind
only to wither, while misery, deceit,
and infamy alone survive.
We weave! We weave!

“The shuttle flies, the loom creaks;
day and night we weave without cease.
Old Germany, your icy shroud
our fingers weave in darkness,
our lips mingling in the cloth
echoes of curses and rage.
We weave! We weave!”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Cuando de noche pienso en Alemania
translations.text:
When at night I think of Germany,
sleep does not descend upon my eyelids;
my eyes do not close, but are wet
with my burning tears.
Time passes; twelve years now
since I last saw my mother;
with absence my longing and sorrow
grow greater every day.
My longing and sorrow grow;
held by a strange enchantment,
at every hour the little old woman
comes to mind—may Heaven keep her.
The poor old woman loves me so
that even in her letters I can see
her hand trembling, and her mother’s heart
stirring there in her breast.
My mother never leaves my thoughts;
twelve years have passed,
twelve slow years of pain
since I held her to my breast.
Germany will endure;
it is a land of sound and sturdy body:
with its strong oaks and lindens
I can always find its dear soil.
If my poor mother did not live there,
my heart would not sigh to return.
Germany will not die, but my mother
may fly to Heaven.
How many, since I left my homeland,
has death kissed with its icy lips!
My poor heart bleeds sadly
when I count them.
And count them I must; each number
adds to my grief, and the dead,
cold and mournful, rolling down,
I believe, O God, upon my wounded breast.
Good God, through my window enters
the calm radiance of the French sun;
my wife comes in, and her smile banishes
my homesick, melancholy memories.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Doto mi vida de una esperanza agónica
translations.text:
Anoint me, hands pierced by a
solid gold nail;
hands hanging from the man,
hands pricked.
I hunger,
hunger for the dream that flows
in the smallest grain of salt.
My whole body sticky
with dirty, golden flies.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: La visión
translations.text:
I lay in darkness, eyelids lowered toward terror,
perhaps at the world’s end, with these sleepless hands,
amid the wind crossing me with scraps of sky.
Then I had no thought; in an immense whiteness
my temples vanished like crowns drained of blood,
and my bones shone like sacred bronze.
You touched that summit where dawn flows softly,
with my hands showing through a sea in magical order.
It was the purest road, and light already solid;
over sleeping waters it slid toward my origins,
breaking my white skin; only its oil gleamed.
My morning self was born, perhaps of earth or sky,
which I had awaited since long ago, and whose shadowed passage
silenced my ear, buzzing like the wind’s nest.
For the first time I was lucid, yet without tongue or echoes,
without tears, discovering notions and golden melodies;
I released a dove, and it sealed my blood in silence.
I understood the brow forming over a vast dream,
like a slow scab over a wound that never stops flowing.
That is all: night made secret bouquets of my arms,
and perhaps my back was already congealing in its own shadow.
I returned to darkness, once more a repressed larva in my brow,
and terror made me rejoice in my heart’s clear songs.
I am sure I touched the ashes of my own death,
those which, within the dream, make my deepest wakefulness.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: La intolerable unión de los despojos
translations.text:
Everything has been consummated
at once.
Like a trumpet
you have split in two,
and a shriek comes out—
not from you,
but from time’s deaf conclusion.

Out comes the ghost
that insisted in our conversations.
Remember?
Remember the sudden crack
of silk?
The uprising of chairs?
The shirt growing ever paler?

You said:
“I came in!”
But no one entered.
A whirl of music consumed the space,
and we remained astonished,
holding up
the burning dome of another world.

Now
the ghost has openings for a mouth
and says nothing.
No one says anything.

Things slowly go dark.
In your fierce gag,
words remain, kisses remain.

No one says anything,
because nothing has meaning.
The irrevocable
is an empty truth
that lies in wait for us
without true reason.

As we look at you,
we look at ourselves,
petrified,
alive!

O form! O crackling
of form,
that frees us from nothingness
at the same time it leads us to it!

Should I praise or
curse
your death
as the endless doubling
of a barely perceptible presence?
I do not know.
My soul is blindfolded.

I only want
to anoint your eyes with
the brightness of my life.

I remember you
like a foaming horse
chewing
the bridle of death;
like a cyclops
fighting a horned wall.
Tender,
hunting a lost star
in your body.

Humble,
caring for a lame dove.
Furious
before the poor man’s empty table.

Have you joined
yourself?
And what is gained
by fulfilling a solitude
more vast?
There,
I know not where,
carving with your teeth
an ivory forest
without any worthy purpose?
You abounded only in
your fellow man.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Envío
translations.text:
Brother:
I will look for you behind the street corners.
And you will not be there.

I will look for you in the cloud of birds.
And you will not be there.

I will look for you in a beggar’s hand.
And you will not be there.

I will look for you, too,
in the Golden Initial of a Book of Prayers.
And you will not be there.

I will look for you in the gnomes’ night.
And you will not be there.

I will look for you in the air inside a music box.
And you will not be there.

(I will look for you in the children’s eyes.
And there you will be.)
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Elegiré una Piedra...
translations.text:
I will choose a stone.
And a tree.

And a cloud.
And I will cry your name
until the blind air that carries you
hears me.
(Softly.)

I will knock on the little window of dew;
I will stretch a cord of hemp and resin;
I will raise your sailor’s linen
up to the First Wind of your Sign,
so the Sea may name you.
(Softly.)

Four birds mourn you;
a burden of children and puppets;
the night jasmine of a Paraguayan courtyard.
And a folk guitar.
(Softly.)

They call you:
every humble thing beneath the sky;
the innocence of a piece of bread;
the handful of salt spilled
on a poor man’s tablecloth;
a horse’s submissive gaze,
and an abandoned dog.
And a letter.
(Softly.)

I, too, have called you,
in my highland night of orange blossoms.
(Softly.)

Only your solitude, now and forever,
will call you, night and day.
Aloud.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Hombre frente al mar
translations.text:
He is like me: I feel him with my anguish and my blood.
Beautiful in sadness, he goes to meet the sea,
so Sun and Wind may air his agony.
Peace on his still brow; his heart in ruins;
he still wants to live, in order to die longer.

He is like me: I see him with my lost eyes;
he too seeks shelter in the sea’s night;
he too bears the broken arc of a flight
over his aged heart.

He goes, like me, dressed in nocturnal solitude.
Both hands outstretched toward the ocean’s murmur,
he asks the sea’s time to free him
from the unceasing blow of waves that shakes
his aged heart, full of shadows.

He is like me: I feel his image as if it were mine,
shaped by the eternal fury
of his inner sea.

Beautiful in sadness,
he tries—in vain—not to burn the sand
with the bitter acid of his tears.

He is like me: I feel as if it were mine,
his aged heart, full of shadows…
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.text:

translations.title: Simple ruego por el ausente esperado
translations.text:
I waited for you:
you were like a brother whose hand one seeks
to press to the hot lips of a wound.

And you were absent, brother: you fell silent
when everyone prayed for your presence.

But your shadow came:
nothing but your shadow, absent brother.

It opened its ancient, still-sealed mouth,
and let this plea for forgiveness for your absence
flower upon its hard lips:
“…I have returned to earth what belonged to earth,
but what I shall be tomorrow remains with you.

“Do not weep for me, brothers: I am among you.
Time no longer carries me in its leagues-long hands,
nor does the shape of space press on my eyes.

“My garment floats above Dawn and Night,
beyond memory.
My transformations seek a purer vessel,
to breathe into me a body that may return to you.”

Your voice fell silent; we felt you shiver with cold,
fearing you might suffer another fall.

As one defending himself against unspeakable anguish,
I murmured, like a prayer, your ineffable plea:

“Time no longer carries me in its leagues-long hands,
nor does the shape of space press on my eyes…”

So be it.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Balada para los árboles ausentes
translations.text:
Along the silver road,
confused among the shadows,
came eight murderers
with newly forged axes.

Across their rustless edges
the night wind passes,
then embraces the foliage
to whisper in secret
that eight murderers are coming
with newly forged axes.

How the clouds are trembling!
O my God, how the stars and birds weep!
How innocent night breaks
its voice of silence
and its silver music!

They bared their torsos,
looked up from below,
and amid the green celebration
each marked his crime.
High toward the sky they raised
the newly forged blades;
when they came down, they roared
through the mouths of their edges.
Neither clouds nor birds
could blind them.

The foliage shudders
as if it were dying;
the stars grow cold
at sight of naked iron,
and dawn’s water comes
to weep with the moon.

The murderers fled,
their axes like mirrors.
The birds no longer have
a place to hang their songs.

The wind goes off sobbing,
carrying its dead leaves,
while silver night breaks
its voice of silence
and its music of moons.

When day came again,
the presence of an absence
wept its sadness in the sun,
a desolate scar.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Federico: te he visto...
translations.text:
Federico:
I have seen you here, seated on a black stone,
facing the sea that stilled its fury on the beach,
while the sun polished your gypsy profile
against the swirling limbo of the sleeping afternoon.

I have seen you so: seated, your shirt open,
your sailor’s bronzed chest scorched,
silencing your ardent guitar’s voices
with the dull cry of a handful of sand.

Our green gypsy, whom death ripened:
a thousand years from now, beside this same stone,
the same bitter sand your hand lifted
will still be weeping your awakened name.

When you knelt upon your own earth,
the sea, which aired your chest with its iodine breath,
fell silent… The music-murmuring shells
suddenly hushed their age-old songs.

Velvet grains of sea sand;
paths of winds carrying dreams away;
nights driven mad by the joy of worlds;
wings bearing their burning music to and fro;
everything—wind and sand, worlds and wings and nights—
weeps bloodied dawns over your clear name.

Federico: the years have dried your flesh;
earthworms have entered it;
but your distant voice, mighty with symbols,
is not dead, like the sea…
Amid albatross flight and a tumult of stars,
your festival of songs turned toward infinity.

A thousand years from now, beside this same stone
that set your figure against the Atlantic curtain,
I will still be waiting for another kindred music
to pierce the limestone labyrinth of my ears.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Sumas
translations.text:
Horse and rider are already two animals.
One plus one,
we say. And we think:
one apple plus one apple,
one glass plus one
glass,
always identical things.

What a change when
one plus one is a Puritan
plus a gamelan,

one jasmine plus one Arab,
a nun and a cliff,
a song and a
mask,
once more a garrison and a maiden,
someone’s hope
plus another’s dream.

From “Reduction of the Infinite,” 2002
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: El fuego
translations.text:
Without him
here
without him.
His fire whispering.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Escribo, pienso, leo
translations.text:
I write
think
read
translate twenty pages
listen to the news
write
write
read.

Where are you
where are you.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Dónde el sueño cumplido
translations.text:
Where is the fulfilled dream
and where the mad love
that all of us,
or some of us,
always
behind the serene mask
ask for on our knees
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Como en la playa virgen...
translations.text:
As on the virgin beach
the wind bends
the slender green reed
that draws
a delicate circle in the sand,
so in me
your memory.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Buscamos
translations.text:
We search
every night,
with effort,
among heavy, suffocating lands,
for that light bird of light
that burns and escapes us
with a moan.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Entre tus brazos
translations.text:
In your arms
in my arms
between the soft sheets
between the night
tender
alone
fierce
between the shadows
between the hours
between
before and after.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: No te amaba...
translations.text:
Poor my love,
you thought
it was like that;
you did not know.
It was richer than
that,
it was poorer than that;
it was life, and you,
with your eyes closed,
saw your nightmares
and said:
“life.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Pasa se va se pierde
translations.text:
It passes, goes, is lost,
does not stop,
flows,
springs endlessly,
slips from our hands,
runs, flies toward its end,
glides,
goes dark,
annihilates itself,
fades,
comes undone,
is over.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Buscamos...
translations.text:
You did not know

Poor my love,
you thought
it was like that;
you did not know.
It was richer than
that,
it was poorer than that;
it was life, and you,
with your eyes closed,
saw your nightmares
and said:
“life.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Poema número 19
translations.text:
I want to die. I do not want
to hear any more bells.

Bells—what a metaphor—
or siren songs,
or fairy tales,
old wives’ tales—come now.

I simply do not want to;
I do not want to hear any more bells.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Decir no
translations.text:
To say no,
to say no,
tie myself to the mast,
but
wishing the wind would overturn it,
that the siren would rise and with her teeth
cut the ropes and drag me to the depths,
saying no no no
while following her.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Aquel amor...
translations.text:
That love,
that one
taken with my fingertips,
that I left, that I forgot,
that love,
now,
in a few lines that
fall from a drawer,
is there,
still there,
still telling me,
it hurts,
it is
still
bleeding.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Después
translations.text:
It is another woman,
perhaps another,
who is recovering
her hair, her dress, her way;
who now regains
her uprightness,
her weight,
and after lustful, tender sessions
leaves through the door whole and pure,
and does not seek to know,
does not need to,
does not want to know
anything about anyone.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: No sos mío no estás...
translations.text:
You are not mine, you are not here
in my life,
by my side;
you do not eat at my table,
nor laugh nor sing,
nor live for me.
We are strangers,
you
and I myself
and my home.
You are a strange guest
who seeks and wants nothing
but a bed
sometimes.

What can I do?
Give it to you.

But I live alone.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Todo es muy simple
translations.text:
Everything is very simple, much
simpler, and yet
there are still moments
when it is too much for me,
when I do not understand,
and I do not know whether to laugh aloud
or cry with fear,
or stay here without tears,
without laughter,
in silence,
accepting my life,
my passage,
my time.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Eso
translations.text:
My weariness,
my anguish,
my joy,
my terror,
my humility,
all my nights,
my nostalgia for the year
nineteen thirty,
my common sense,
my rebellion.

My disdain,
my cruelty and my grief,
my abandonment,
my weeping,
my agony,
my inescapable and painful inheritance,
my suffering,
in the end,
my poor life.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: No te amaba
translations.text:
I did not love you;
I do not love you;
I know well that I do not,
that I do not,
that it is the hour,
the light,
the summer afternoon.

I know it,
but I love you.
Now I love you,
today,
this afternoon I love you,
as I loved you on other afternoons,
desperately,
with blind love,
with anger,
with the saddest knowledge,
beyond desire,
or illusion,
or waiting,
and waiting all the same,
waiting for you,
seeing
you come,
at last,
you arrive,
just passing through.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Cuándo ya noches mías
translations.text:
When, my nights,
you will be unknown and untouched,
unbrushed.

When, my scents, you will be unmixed,
unviolated.

When I will be a cold star
and not a flower in a colorful bouquet.

And when my life,
my arduous life,
in solitude,
like a slow drop
always wanting to fall
and always held,
loading, filling,
with itself, trembling,
hastening its brightness
and its return to the river.

Then without trembling or light,
falling darkly.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: El amor
translations.text:
A bird sings to me
and I sing to it;
it warbles in my ear
and I warble back.
It wounds me and I bleed for it;
it shatters me,
I break it;
it undoes me,
I smash it;
it helps me,
I lift it up;
I fill everything with peace,
everything with war,
everything with hate, with love;
and unbound,
its voice moans and I moan,
it laughs and I laugh,
it looks at me and I look at it,
it speaks and I speak,
it loves me and I love it—
this is not a matter of love,
we give our lives—
and it asks of me and I ask of it,
it conquers me and I conquer it,
it ends me and I end it.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: El mar
translations.text:
So arduously the sea,
so arduously,
the slow, immense sea,
so long within itself, so tired,
the deep, eternal sea.

Slow sea, deep sea,
immense, profound sea…

So slowly, deeply, so long, so much,
insistent and tired being falling
like an endless weeping,
heavily,
tenaciously dying…

It grows calm from the depths,
grows wisely,
slowly, deeply, at length,
with measured pace,
sea,
arduous, weary sea,
Father of my silence.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Desnudez total
translations.text:
Already in total nakedness,
a strange absence
of processes, formulas, methods,
flower by flower,
being by being,
even with knowledge,
and a silent fall without purpose.

Anguish has become
barely a flavor;
pain no longer fits,
sadness does not suffice.

A form lasting without meaning,
a color,
a being merely there,
and a senseless wait.

Already in total nakedness:
wisdom,
final, singular, and cold.

Light by light,
being by being,
almost an amoeba,
form, thirst, duration,
rejected light.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.

translations.title: Concédeme esos cielos, esos mundos dormidos
translations.text:
Grant me those heavens, those sleeping worlds,
the weight of silence, that arch, that abandonment;
set my hands alight,
deepen my life
with the sweet gift I ask of you.

Give me the somber light, passionate and steady,
of those distant heavens, the harmony
of those sealed worlds;
give me the silent limit, the arrested
outline of those shadow moons,
their contained song.

You, the denied one, give everything;
you, the powerful one, ask;
you, the silent one, give me the sweetest gift
of that immediate, senseless honey.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish source; no separate editorial review occurred.
